targetTexts.1: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a fool whose lips are perverse.
targetTexts.2: Even zeal is no good without knowledge, and he who hurries his footsteps misses the mark.
targetTexts.3: A man’s own folly subverts his way, yet his heart rages against the LORD.
targetTexts.4: Wealth attracts many friends, but a poor man is deserted by his friend.
targetTexts.5: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who utters lies will not escape.
targetTexts.6: Many seek the favor of the prince, and everyone is a friend of the gift giver.
targetTexts.7: All the brothers of a poor man hate him—how much more do his friends avoid him! He may pursue them with pleading, but they are nowhere to be found.
targetTexts.8: He who acquires wisdom loves himself; one who safeguards understanding will find success.
targetTexts.9: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who pours out lies will perish.
targetTexts.10: Luxury is unseemly for a fool—how much worse for a slave to rule over princes!
targetTexts.11: A man’s insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to overlook an offense.
targetTexts.12: A king’s rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
targetTexts.13: A foolish son is his father’s ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping.
targetTexts.14: Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.
targetTexts.15: Laziness brings on deep sleep, and an idle soul will suffer hunger.
targetTexts.16: He who keeps a commandment preserves his soul, but he who is careless in his ways will die.
targetTexts.17: Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender.
targetTexts.18: Discipline your son, for in that there is hope; do not be party to his death.
targetTexts.19: A man of great anger must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do so again.
targetTexts.20: Listen to counsel and accept discipline, that you may be wise the rest of your days.
targetTexts.21: Many plans are in a man’s heart, but the purpose of the LORD will prevail.
targetTexts.22: The desire of a man is loving devotion; better to be poor than a liar.
targetTexts.23: The fear of the LORD leads to life, that one may rest content, without visitation from harm.
targetTexts.24: The slacker buries his hand in the dish; he will not even bring it back to his mouth.
targetTexts.25: Strike a mocker, and the simple will beware; rebuke the discerning man, and he will gain knowledge.
targetTexts.26: He who assaults his father or evicts his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
targetTexts.27: If you cease to hear instruction, my son, you will stray from the words of knowledge.
targetTexts.28: A corrupt witness mocks justice, and a wicked mouth swallows iniquity.
targetTexts.29: Judgments are prepared for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools.
